messages.author: c03adc32d52e7037
messages.subject: camOp table construction
parts: hello, how could you declare discontinuous periods of inactivity or inoperability of a camera? for the construction of a camOp table. I have 3 years of sampling only in the dry season. Thank you

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: camOp table construction
parts:
Hi, 
the next version will include a "sessionCol" argument in the function cameraOperation, but it is not out yet.

The best strategy until then depends on how your data were collected and what you are trying to do. Can you please share how your cameras were set up (i.e., multiple cameras per station?) and what analyses you wish to conduct?

Some ideas though. For each camera / station that was operated discontinuously, you could:

1) have multiple entries in the station column of your camera trap information table for the cameras
2) have multiple entries in the camera column of your camera trap information table (same station, different cameras)
3) have one entry in your camera trap information table per camera and use the "Problem1_from" / "Problem1_to" way of declaring periods on inactivity.

Let me know and I'll be able to answer more precisely. 
Best,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: camOp table construction
parts:
Hi,

it depends what you mean by issues. Technically you can do it. What is more relevant is the assumptions that are implied, most importantly the closure assumption. It will not hold over many years.

Also, using multi-sessions allows you to estimate additional parameters (extinction and colonization probabilities) and how they are affected by covariates.

The best choice depends on the study design and how it relates to the assumptions of the models.

See the colext vignette in unmarked for some thorough explanations and examples.

Cheers,

Jürgen
